A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEGS2 with the same authors, core framework and principal experiments. All pages are readable, including v3's Appendix A.1–A.5; v1 ends with references and has no appendix. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, rendering-memory and ablation results on three benchmark datasets, alongside WebGL device demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds reflective-scene evaluations, device comparisons, training-time measurements, sensitivity analyses and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: The SG representation, joint pruning objective and color compensation remain. v3 retains only dynamic-range-based lobe selection from v1's two alternatives and specifies importance-based opacity selection across all scenes in A.2. Algorithm 1 also replaces the shared penalty coefficient with weighted opacity and sharpness coefficients. These refine the reported procedure without introducing a new framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds the Shiny Blender Real evaluation on Garden, Sedan and Toycar (Table 11), plus explicit highly specular and dense-transparency test cases (Figure 8). These substantially extend the tested material conditions. The original Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples and DeepBlending coverage remains; its new per-scene breakdowns are not additional datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LightGaussian, LocoGS and MaskGaussian while retaining the earlier comparators. Table 11 introduces comparisons with Ref-NeRF, ENVIDR, 2DGS, GShader, R3DG, 3DGS-DR and Ref-Gaussian. The expanded WebGL comparison includes GaussianSpa. The earlier Scaffold-GS/HAC++ comparison is retained as v3 Table 4.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs cover storage size, training duration on RTX 3090/4090, expanded WebGL device configurations and rendering-failure categories, and a controlled primitive/lobe-budget sweep (Tables 9–12; Figure 6). The original image-quality metrics and static/rendering VRAM measurement definitions remain. Newly disclosed pruning settings do not establish changes to the original training protocol.

E4.justification: The original pruning ablations remain unchanged numerically in v3 Table 2, formerly Table 4. v3 adds scene-wise lobe-allocation analysis, pruning-budget sensitivity, challenging-material success/failure cases, visual ablations and a Playroom texture case study (Figures 5, 6, 8, 9 and 14). These test additional questions about allocation, sensitivity and failure behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new mean columns summarize scenes rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive per-scene, reflective-scene, device, storage, training-time and sensitivity results. Existing entries also change: the first Ours row, now labeled HQ, changes on Tanks & Temples from 23.57 to 23.45 PSNR, 0.855 to 0.853 SSIM, 59 to 51 MB static VRAM and 209 to 211 MB rendering VRAM. Figure 1 replaces 3DGS's Dimensity 9400+ N/A with 6.6 FPS. Most original aggregate and ablation values remain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an augmented-Lagrangian derivation of the optimization updates and a spherical-integral derivation of the color-compensation solution, whereas v1 largely states the updates and final solution. It also explicitly derives delta_o = delta times rho_o and delta_s = delta times rho_s, matching the revised pseudocode. This substantially expands the mathematical support for existing components.

C1.justification: v3 refines the novelty framing by explicitly crediting SG-Splatting's earlier hybrid SH/SG approach and identifying MEGS2's contribution as fully standalone, arbitrarily oriented and prunable SG color modeling. The central joint-pruning contribution and headline 50% static and 40% rendering VRAM reduction claims remain.

C2.justification: The limitations concerning unoptimized dynamic VRAM and complex highlights are retained within the conclusion. v3 adds concrete applicability qualifications for highly specular surfaces and dense transparency (Figure 8), and attributes Playroom speckles to ground-truth shadows and image roughness (Figure 14). Figure 1 also qualifies 3DGS's mobile failure claim to some platforms.

D1.justification: A.2 newly specifies 10,000 memory-constrained optimization iterations, a 50-iteration interval, penalty 0.0005, sharpness threshold 1 and the opacity importance calculation. v3 also documents LocoGS initialization, the WebGL viewer's origin and GPU-specific training times. Its reproducibility statement promises a future release of renderer, training and evaluation code; it does not establish current availability.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly positions its standalone representation relative to SG-Splatting's hybrid design. It adds references for ADMM, LightGaussian, MaskGaussian, LocoGS and the WebGL viewer, and removes the end-to-end rate-distortion Gaussian representation reference. Most related-work discussion and the rendering-memory-versus-storage positioning remain.

P1.justification: The main text is substantially condensed and reorganized: the method overview and preliminaries are shortened, experimental setup and analyses are rewritten, detailed evaluation information moves to A.2, and limitations merge into the conclusion. v3 introduces a structured appendix and reproducibility, ethics and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v3 expands and reformats Table 1 with explicit HQ/LM labels, relocates the parameter-cost and HAC++ tables to the appendix, wraps the ablation table beside text, and redraws the color-model plot. It adds lobe-distribution and sensitivity charts, per-scene tables, failure-case panels, visual ablations and extensive device-image grids.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the central memory-efficiency and edge-rendering claims through broader comparisons, practical cost measurements, sensitivity tests and explicit failure cases. The derivations and pruning details also address important gaps in v1's methodological transparency. Some new reporting needs reconciliation: for example, Table 6's 3DGS static VRAM values of 397 and 752 MB do not average to Table 1's 370 MB. These inconsistencies limit confidence in individual entries, but the overall gains in inspectability and validation remain substantial.
